Training DetailsWe construct our training data from the xlam-IC dialogue dataset, where $30 \%$ of the samples are replaced with error-correction augmented dialogues. We explore two adaptation strategies for the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model: LoRA(Hu et al., 2O21) and full-parameter finetuning. More details are provided in Appendix E.

BaselinesFor comprehensive comparison, we evaluate representative tool-augmented LLMs, including xLAM-7b-fc-r (trained on the xlamfunction-calling-6Ok dataset but without intent clarification) (Liu et al., 2024), gorilla-openfunctionsv2 (Patil et al., 2023), and ToolLLaMA-2-7b-v2 (Qin et al., 2O24), as well as an intent clarification model, Mistral-Interact (Qian et al., 2O24). In addition,we evaluate major LLM series,includingMistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3,LLaMA(3-8B/70BInstruct), Qwen (2.5-7B/72B-Instruct), DeepSeekV3, Claude (3.5-Haiku/Sonnet), and GPT (3.5, 4, 40-mini, 4o). All models use a standardized evaluation prompt (see Appendix F.1).

We fine-tune two variants of the Qwen2.5-7BInstruct model on the xlam-IC dataset, in which $30 \%$ of the samples are replaced with errorcorrection augmented dialogues. Both variants are trained using the LLaMA-Factory framework (Zheng et al., 2024).

For LoRA fine-tuning,we set the LoRA rank to 8. We use an initial learning rate of 1.Oe-4, a warm-up ratio of O.1,and a cosine learning rate scheduler. Training is conducted on $4 { \times } \mathrm { R T X } 3 0 9 0$ (24GB) GPUs for 3 epochs with a batch size of 64.

For full-parameter fine-tuning,we use an initial learning rate of 1.41e-5 under the same schedule. Training is conducted on ${ 8 \times { \mathrm { R T X } } }$ A6000 (48GB) GPUs for 3 epochs with a batch size of 64.
